narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: Tells the story; reads all narration and genealogies.

joseph-the-patriarch.name: Joseph
joseph-the-patriarch.note: Jacob's favoured son; candid dreamer at seventeen, then upright slave and calm interpreter of dreams in prison.

josephs-brothers.name: Joseph's brothers
josephs-brothers.note: The sons of Jacob speaking together; envious and scornful of Joseph, then deceiving their father.

jacob.name: Jacob (Israel)
jacob.note: The aged patriarch; fond of Joseph, rebuking his dream, then broken with grief.

reuben.name: Ruben
reuben.note: Jacob's eldest; tries to save Joseph, then distraught at finding the pit empty.

judah.name: Juda
judah.note: Jacob's fourth son; pragmatic in selling Joseph, peremptory as head of his house, then owning his fault.

man-at-sichem.name: Man at Sichem
man-at-sichem.note: A stranger who finds Joseph wandering in the field and directs him to Dothain.

1.t: And Jacob dwelt in the land of Chanaan, wherein his father sojourned.

2.t: And these are his generations: Joseph, when he was sixteen years old, was feeding the flock with his brethren, being but a boy: and he was with the sons of Bala and of Zelpha his father's wives: and he accused his brethren to his father of a most wicked crime.

3.t: Now Israel loved Joseph above all his sons, because he had him in his old age: and he made him a coat of divers colours.

4.t: And his brethren seeing that he was loved by his father, more than all his sons, hated hem, and could not speak peaceably to him.

5.t: Now it fell out also that he told his brethren a dream, that he had dreamed: which occasioned them to hate him the more.

6.t: Hear my dream which I dreamed.

7.t: I thought we were binding sheaves in the field: and my sheaf arose as it were, and stood, and your sheaves standing about bowed down before my sheaf.

8.t: Shalt thou be our king? or shall we be subject to thy dominion?
Therefore this matter of his dreams and words ministered nourishment to their envy and hatred.

9.t: He dreamed also another dream, which he told his brethren, saying:
I saw in a dream, as it were the sun, and the moon, and eleven stars worshipping me.

10.t: And when he had told this to his father, and brethren, his father rebuked him and said:
What meaneth this dream that thou hast dreamed? shall I and thy mother, and thy brethren worship thee upon the earth?

11.t: His brethren therefore envied him: but his father considered the thing with himself.

12.t: And when his brethren abode in Sechem, feeding their father's flocks,

13.t: Thy brethren feed the sheep in Sichem: come, I will send thee to them.

14.t: Go, and see if all things be well with thy brethren, and the cattle: and bring me word again what is doing.
So being sent from the vale of Hebron, he came to Sichem:

15.t: And a man found him there wandering in the field, and asked what he sought.

16.t: I seek my brethren, tell me where they feed the flocks.

17.t: And the man said to him:
They are departed from this place: for I heard them say: Let us go to Dothain.
And Joseph went forward after his brethren, and found them in Dothain.

18.t: And when they saw him afar off, before he came nigh them, they thought to kill him:

20.t: Come, let us kill him, and cast him into some old pit: and we will say: Some evil beast hath devoured him: and then it shall appear what his dreams avail him:

21.t: And Ruben hearing this, endeavoured to deliver him out of their hands, and said:

22.t: Do not take away his life, nor shed his blood: but cast him into this pit, that is in the wilderness, and keep your hands harmless:
now he said this, being desirous to deliver him out of their hands and to restore him to his father.

23.t: And as soon as he came to his brethren, they forthwith stript him of his outside coat, that was of divers colours:

24.t: And cast him into an old pit where there was not water.

25.t: And sitting down to eat bread, they saw some Ismaelites on their way coming from Galaad, with their camels, carrying spices, and balm, and myrrh to Egypt.

26.t: And Juda said to his brethren:
What will it profit us to kill our brother, and conceal his blood?

27.t: It is better that he be sold to the Ismaelites, and that our hands be not defiled: for he is our brother and our flesh.
His brethren agreed to his words.

28.t: And when the Madianite merchants passed by, they drew him out of the pit, and sold him to the Ismaelites, for twenty pieces of silver: and they led him into Egypt.

29.t: And Ruben returning to the pit, found not the boy:

30.t: And rending his garments he went to his brethren, and said:
The boy doth not appear, and whither shall I go?

31.t: And they took his coat, and dipped it in the blood of a kid, which they had killed:

32.t: Sending some to carry it to their father, and to say:
This we have found: see whether it be thy son's coat, or not.
32.q: the message the brothers send by messengers; given to the brothers who composed it rather than a separate messenger voice

33.t: And the father acknowledging it, said:
It is my son's coat, an evil wild beast hath eaten him, a beast hath devoured Joseph.

34.t: And tearing his garments, he put on sackcloth, mourning for his son a long time.

35.t: And all his children being gathered together to comfort their father in his sorrow, he would not receive comfort, but said:
I will go down to my son into hell, mourning.

36.t: The Madianites sold Joseph in Egypt to Putiphar, an eunuch of Pharao, captain of the soldiers.
